title: AWS provider: HTML extraction profiles, live-derived fixtures, and a coverage declaration
objective: Add the fourth of six F008 providers. AWS publishes THREE distinct free-offer kinds - Always Free (perpetual), a time-limited introductory tier, and trials/credits - and only the first could ever be perpetual. The central risk of this slice is conflating them, or claiming an AWS service is free on evidence AWS does not actually serve in HTML. Every published fact must be pinned either to a real live table row or to a verbatim same-document prose block; nothing may be synthesized to satisfy the extractor.
measured_premise: P1 MEASURED 2026-08-14 (live, HTTP 200): the AWS documentation host (docs.aws.amazon.com) serves client-rendered shells for its guide pages. The Billing user guide's free-tier page (path /awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/billing-free-tier.html) served 1166 bytes and the Lambda developer guide's billing page (path /lambda/latest/dg/lambda-billing.html) served 1083 bytes. Parsed with the repository's own _DocumentCollector, BOTH yield 0 tables, 0 document blocks and 0 heading blocks: the content is not in the served HTML. These pages are therefore NOT used, and that is reported rather than worked around. The host is deliberately NOT added to scripts/url-allowlist.txt, because no committed source cites it.

P2 MEASURED (live, HTTP 200): https://aws.amazon.com/free/ contains exactly ONE <table>, whose live header row is ['Benefits', 'Free plan', 'Paid plan'] with 6 body rows. It is a genuine <thead>-delimited table, so a matrix profile over it reads live structure and synthesizes nothing.

P3 MEASURED (live, HTTP 200): https://aws.amazon.com/free/free-tier-faqs/ contains ZERO <table> elements and 131 document blocks. https://aws.amazon.com/free/terms/ contains ZERO <table> elements and 118 document blocks. Both are therefore mode='assertions' and declare no table selector; no anchor table is fabricated for either.

P4 MEASURED (live, HTTP 200): AWS SERVICE PRICING PAGES ARE NOT MATRIX-EXTRACTABLE. Across 13 probed pricing pages (lambda, dynamodb, s3, cloudfront, cognito, sns, cloudwatch, lightsail, step-functions, ec2, api-gateway, sqs, amplify) essentially no free-tier table carries a <th> header row: _header_row returns 'expected one header row, found 0' for 4/4 Lambda tables, 3/3 DynamoDB tables and 8/8 S3 tables. Only Step Functions and Amplify expose a header row at all and neither of those tables is a free-tier table. Per-service free-tier extraction on AWS must therefore be assertion-based, not matrix-based.

P5 MEASURED (live): Lambda's free-tier numbers appear in served HTML ONLY inside repeated worked pricing examples ('the free tier provides 400,000 GB-s' occurs in 6 separate blocks). There is no unique block stating the Lambda free-tier allowance, so Lambda is REJECTED as a source rather than pinned to an ambiguous block.

P6 MEASURED (live): https://aws.amazon.com/free/free-tier-faqs/ states VERBATIM, in a block occurring exactly once, 'Yes, you are required to provide a valid payment method to sign up for an AWS account, whether you choose a free plan or a paid plan.' That single block names the FREE PLAN explicitly, so requires_card=True for the free-plan offer is quoted, not composed from two blocks. This is the UNFAVOURABLE finding and it is published.

P7 MEASURED (live): the same page states VERBATIM, exactly once, 'If you exceed the free usage limits, your account will begin incurring charges at the standard pay-as-you-go service rates ...'. This is carried whole as a note on the free-plan offer. It is NOT converted into exhaustion_behaviour for that offer, because the same block states that a free-plan account sees no charges on its bills; the free plan's own exhaustion is taken from the block that describes it directly.

P8 CORRECTED (live): an earlier reading concluded that AWS NEVER describes an Always Free offer in a block of its own. That was WRONG, and wrong in the omission-favouring direction. It holds only for the Free Tier HUB pages, where the 'always free' vocabulary appears solely inside blocks that also grant the $200 credit, inside a PAID-PLAN answer, or as a question heading -- so none of the three hub sources emits always_free. Widening the sweep to service pricing pages found AWS stating it plainly: https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/pricing/ says, in a block of its own, 'The Step Functions Free Tier does not automatically expire at the end of your 12 month AWS Free Tier term, and is available to both existing and new AWS customers indefinitely.' That satisfies DATA_MODEL rule 1 by quotation, so aws_step_functions_free_tier is always_free -- and the same page says 'You are charged per state transition above the free tier', so it is STILL Z1. Perpetual does not mean Z0.

P9 CORRECTED (live): FOUR blocks on https://aws.amazon.com/free/terms/ occur TWICE, not three as first counted (the resource-reclaim, no-rollover, offer-termination and region-aggregation clauses each appear verbatim in both the current and the Legacy sections). They are REPORTED and deliberately NOT pinned; both occurrences are retained in the fixture so the fixture reproduces the live ambiguity, and a test proves that pinning one yields ambiguous_assertion.

P10 MEASURED (live): every block this slice DOES pin occurs EXACTLY ONCE in its live document within its scope, verified by parsing the live bytes with _DocumentCollector and counting whole-block normalised equality.

P11 MEASURED (live, HTTP 200): https://aws.amazon.com/robots.txt has a 'User-agent: *' group. Its only /free/ Disallow rules are '/free/cloud-computing-free-tier/' and '/free/databases-free-tier/'. None of /free/, /free/free-tier-faqs/, /free/terms/ or /dynamodb/pricing/ is disallowed, so automated retrieval of the four cited pages is permitted.

P12 MEASURED (repository): docs/DATA_MODEL.md 'Choosing between always_free and recurring_quota' rule 1 requires an indefinitely available zero-priced plan/tier/SKU. No AWS page in this slice states one for DynamoDB; the DynamoDB pricing page identifies a free allowance granted 'each month' on a service that is itself metered, which is rule 2, so aws_dynamodb_free_tier emits recurring_quota.

P13 MEASURED (repository, base 80c1684): app/classify/engine.py gate 4 precedes gate 5, so an offer whose requires_card or has_paid_dependencies is unknown classifies UNKNOWN rather than Z2. Three of this slice's four offers therefore classify UNKNOWN, and that is the honest outcome of not inventing card facts.
services_covered_and_why: AWS Free Tier (https://aws.amazon.com/free/) - chosen because it is the ONLY AWS page in the sweep that publishes free-tier facts in a genuine <thead> table, so it is the one place a matrix profile reads live structure. It also carries a single multi-sentence block stating the $200 credit and the 6-month window.

AWS Free Tier free plan (https://aws.amazon.com/free/free-tier-faqs/) - chosen because it is fully server-rendered and carries SEVEN distinct multi-sentence blocks that are each scoped to the free plan: its purpose, its expiry, what happens at expiry, the payment-method requirement, why the payment method is required, eligibility, and credit expiry. It is the strongest evidence page AWS serves.

AWS 12 Month Free Tier (https://aws.amazon.com/free/terms/) - chosen as the deliberate TIME-LIMITED control and because the AWS Free Tier Terms are the authoritative legal statement of the offer kinds. Its Legacy section names the 12-month introductory period explicitly and states its duration and its new-customer-only eligibility in blocks that are each unique live.

Amazon DynamoDB (https://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/pricing/) - chosen as a real SERVICE, because it states its free allowance as a unique intro block plus a five-item list of per-metric allowances rather than only inside repeated worked examples.

Amazon API Gateway (https://aws.amazon.com/api-gateway/pricing/) - chosen because ONE block carries the allowance, a 12-month bound AND the overage consequence together: 'If you exceed this number of calls per month, you will be charged the API Gateway usage rates.' It is the clearest time-limited service offer AWS serves.

AWS Step Functions (https://aws.amazon.com/step-functions/pricing/) - added after P8 was corrected. It is the ONE genuinely perpetual AWS offer found, stated in a block of its own, AND its overage is billed, so it demonstrates the product's central lesson: perpetual is not Z0.

REJECTED: AWS Lambda (free-tier numbers only inside 6 repeated pricing examples, see P5). REJECTED: the two docs.aws.amazon.com guide pages (client-rendered, see P1). REJECTED for now but a strong next candidate: Amazon Cognito, which DOES publish unique free-tier blocks (10,000 MAU, stated indefinite); it was left out to keep the covered set small enough that every claim is fully evidenced and fixture-backed, and auth-identity is declared unknown with that reason recorded. REJECTED: S3, CloudFront, SNS, CloudWatch, Lightsail, EC2, SQS and Amplify pricing pages (no header-row free-tier table and no unique free-tier prose block naming an allowance, see P4).

acceptance_criteria: A1: every profile extracts successfully from the LIVE page, not only from the committed fixture, with the fact set and per-source evidence count reported.
A2 LIVE -> FIXTURE (primary direction): every live target-table row and every pinned live block appears in the corresponding fixture, reported as counts with the live-primary direction called out.
A3 FIXTURE -> LIVE (supporting direction only): every fixture row and pinned block occurs in the live document. This direction may never carry a pass alone.

A4: capture.json explicitly discloses every deletion inside an extracted table (expected: none), every non-target table removed, the measured live table count, and every live block that occurs more than once and was therefore not pinned.
A5: no synthesized table anywhere. Three of four profiles are mode='assertions', declare no table selector, and their fixtures contain zero <table> elements and say so.

A6: the three AWS offer kinds are never conflated, and nothing time-limited or credit-backed can reach Z0, verified by running the REAL classifier. A POSITIVE CONTROL proves the same sweep can observe a Z0, so the zero count is a measurement rather than a vacuous pass.
A7: requires_card is asserted ONLY where a single verbatim block states it. It is True for the free-plan offer and deliberately UNKNOWN elsewhere, with the reason recorded.

A8: mutation tests prove each guard. Each mutation anchor matches EXACTLY ONCE, the patched line is printed, the target error is shown UNPRODUCIBLE on an input that should raise it, a collateral check confirms a healthy document still extracts, and the fixture is restored byte-exactly proved by BLOB HASH, never numstat.
A9: any test parametrized over a discovery helper is accompanied by a NON-VACUITY guard that is not itself parametrized over that discovery.
A10: the classifier verdict is recorded for every offer added.
A11: the full test suite and scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit are run, and it is stated whether they ran against a real PostgreSQL.
A12: the diff is limited to approved files, agent-state/feature_list.json is byte-identical to base, apps/web is zero-diff, and the pull request remains DRAFT.
verification_plan: Re-derive origin/main with git ls-remote before branching and again immediately before reporting.
State a prediction BEFORE each measurement and record where the prediction was wrong.
Drive the real HtmlDocAdapter over LIVE bytes and over the committed fixture, and compare fact sets and evidence selectors.
Judge STRUCTURE, never digest: aws.amazon.com serves per-build markup, so a live digest is not reproducible across fetches.
Run any filtered git diff UNFILTERED first as a positive control, and quote "$base..HEAD" so PowerShell does not split at the dot.
Prove fixture restoration after mutation by git hash-object against git rev-parse ref:path, never by numstat.
Never read an exit code through a truncating pipeline; confirm any alarming result by a second method.
Open a draft PR and read its job status directly with gh rather than assuming the documented CI baseline.
negative_tests: A reworded pinned block must REJECT the document with assertion_not_found, not silently publish a stale value.
A truncated pinned block must REJECT: whole-block normalised equality means a prefix is not a match.
A deleted pinned block must REJECT.
A duplicated pinned block must REJECT with ambiguous_assertion.
Pinning one of the three blocks AWS publishes TWICE on the terms page must REJECT with ambiguous_assertion, proving the decision not to pin them was necessary rather than stylistic.
An undeclared matrix row added to the live plan-comparison table must REJECT with unknown_matrix_rows.
A removed mapped row must REJECT with missing_matrix_rows.
A renamed tier column must REJECT with table_not_found.
A duplicated target table must REJECT with ambiguous_table.
Whitespace and entity noise inside a mapped row label must NOT reject: normalisation is intended behaviour and a false positive here would teach authors to loosen the guard.
An extra body column that leaves the header intact must NOT reject.
Neither trial nor new_customer_credit may reach Z0 on any classifier path, including the hypothetical where every billing gate is explicitly clear.
data_implications: No migration and no schema change. This slice adds provider configuration data, extraction profiles, and test fixtures only. The coverage declaration writes no rows by itself; it is validated config.
security_privacy: Adds one new official documentation host (aws.amazon.com) to the URL allowlist. No credentials, no new dependency, no network access from the test suite (every fixture test runs through FixtureFetcher). Live retrieval happened only during authoring and is recorded in each capture.json.
portability: Standard library only. The profiles are declarative data consumed by the existing engine; no adapter code changes.
z0_risk: Direct and high. AWS is the provider most able to produce a false $0 claim, because it markets three different free-offer kinds under one 'Free Tier' name and only one of them could ever be perpetual. This slice publishes the unfavourable facts - a payment method is required to open any AWS account, exceeding a free allowance begins incurring charges at standard rates, the free plan expires and the account is closed - so the classifier withholds Z0 for every AWS offer it adds.
